beats.narration_slice: Ancient maps show the waterway between Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.
beats.visual: An engraved papyrus map spread across a wooden table, showing a stylized ancient waterway between two landmasses with ships and compass markings, without readable labels.
beats.purpose: show the historical geography of the gulf region through ancient cartography
beats.visual_fingerprint: top-down parchment map composition with tiny sailing ships, carved coastline lines, and archival table setting
beats.continuity: moves from the opened history book into the first historical map discovery

beats.narration_slice: Greek and Roman writers recorded names connected to Persia.
beats.visual: Ancient scrolls and a carved writing tablet beside a classical ink pot, with a small illustrated Mediterranean scholar silhouette studying records.
beats.purpose: show ancient written records connecting names to Persia
beats.visual_fingerprint: side-angle scroll archive scene with classical tablet, ink tools, and scholar silhouette under warm candlelight
beats.continuity: same archival world but shifts from maps to written evidence

beats.narration_slice: Many historical maps label it the Persian Gulf.
beats.visual: A layered collection of aged maps from different centuries stacked together, with repeated highlighted coastline shapes and decorative historical cartography marks.
beats.purpose: show the long tradition of historical map naming
beats.visual_fingerprint: angled stack of antique maps with layered edges, highlighted water shape, and engraved border details
beats.continuity: continues the map theme while expanding from one map to many eras

beats.narration_slice: Arab communities often use the name Arabian Gulf today.
beats.visual: A symbolic modern Gulf coastal scene in engraving style showing regional boats, ports, and community silhouettes around the same waterway, with no political signs or text.
beats.purpose: show present-day regional usage of another name
beats.visual_fingerprint: coastal harbor illustration with traditional boats, community figures, and blue water framed by papyrus edges
beats.continuity: moves from historical maps into a present-day human perspective

beats.narration_slice: The naming debate reflects modern regional identity.
beats.visual: Two groups of symbolic coastal objects from different traditions placed around the same engraved gulf map, showing shared geography and different perspectives.
beats.purpose: explain that names can represent identity and memory
beats.visual_fingerprint: balanced overhead composition with divided cultural artifacts surrounding one central waterway illustration
beats.continuity: connects community usage to the idea of identity

beats.narration_slice: Countries around the gulf choose different names publicly.
beats.visual: An engraved globe beside several small coastline markers around the gulf region, each marker showing different symbolic emblems rather than text.
beats.purpose: show different official choices around the same location
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide desk composition with globe, regional markers, and scattered diplomatic-style parchment pieces
beats.continuity: expands from identity to national perspectives

beats.narration_slice: Iran officially uses Persian Gulf in geography.
beats.visual: A historical geography book page showing an engraved coastline illustration being examined by a hand in gardening gloves, with no readable words.
beats.purpose: show Iran's geographic naming convention through a geography reference
beats.visual_fingerprint: close-up book page with gloved hand, engraved coastline, and garden shelf background
beats.continuity: returns to the gardener investigating through books

beats.narration_slice: Several Arab states publicly use Arabian Gulf.
beats.visual: A second open reference book with coastal illustrations and regional maritime symbols, viewed from above in the same engraved style.
beats.purpose: show another public naming convention through regional references
beats.visual_fingerprint: top-down open book scene with different maritime symbols, darker papyrus tones, and no visible labels
beats.continuity: keeps the investigation format while presenting another perspective

beats.narration_slice: The Strait of Hormuz links the gulf to open waters.
beats.visual: An engraved maritime route illustration showing ships passing through a narrow strait between landforms toward a wider sea.
beats.purpose: explain the geographic connection of the Strait of Hormuz
beats.visual_fingerprint: bird's-eye nautical illustration with narrow passage, sailing ships, and expanding ocean composition
beats.continuity: shifts from names back to physical geography

beats.narration_slice: The answer depends on history, politics, and usage.
beats.visual: The gardener places three engraved objects beside the map: an old scroll, a compass, and community artifacts, forming a balanced triangle.
beats.purpose: show the three factors that shape the naming answer
beats.visual_fingerprint: garden table still life with scroll, compass, artifacts, and central map under golden daylight
beats.continuity: brings the investigation together around the gardener

beats.narration_slice: International geography commonly recognizes Persian Gulf as the established name.
beats.visual: A grand engraved atlas resting open with a globe and historical cartography tools around it, emphasizing a broad geographic reference.
beats.purpose: show the commonly recognized geographic naming tradition
beats.visual_fingerprint: formal atlas display with globe, ruler, and aged map tools in a museum-like papyrus setting
beats.continuity: moves from factors to the broader geographic conclusion

beats.narration_slice: These names show how places carry memory and meaning.
beats.visual: The gardener closes the history book beside the weathered map leaf marker, with the gulf illustration softly glowing on the final page.
beats.purpose: show that place names preserve stories and memories
beats.visual_fingerprint: quiet garden shelf closing scene with gardener, worn book, map marker, and warm evening papyrus light
beats.continuity: returns to the opening garden discovery for a reflective ending
